name: dead-letter-queue
title: Dead-letter undeliverable outbox messages
body:
## Motivation

When the broker rejected `payments.refunded` messages for a few hours last week (the consumer's schema hadn't been deployed yet), the outbox retried every one of them once a second until the deploy went out, and the logs were nothing but `outbox delivery failed` (PAY-226). There is also no way to see which messages are stuck without opening the database. Messages that keep failing should back off, and after a few attempts get out of the way somewhere an operator can look at them and send them again.

## Changes

- Failed deliveries now back off on a schedule defined as data, `BACKOFF_SECONDS = [1, 5, 30, 120, 600]`, and the error message is kept on the row in a new `outbox.last_error` column.
- After `MAX_ATTEMPTS` failures a message is moved to a new `dead_letters` table with the outbox id, topic, payload, number of attempts and the reason it failed, and logged at `error`.
- Restructured `deliver` so each row gets one update that records the attempt and its outcome, instead of separate success and failure updates. `drain` no longer takes a `limit`: the backoff now decides when a message is retried.
- `GET /admin/dead-letters` lists dead letters, newest first, and `POST /admin/dead-letters/:id/retry` puts one back into the outbox under its original id so it is delivered on the next drain. Both sit behind `x-admin-key` with the other admin routes.
- The `payments.<status>` message now includes the `customer` (email and card last 4) that Acme sends on payment events, so support can tell whose payment a dead letter is about and receipts can stop looking it up (PAY-231).
- README documents the retry schedule and the new endpoints.

## Testing

- New `app.inject` tests: the listing returns a dead letter with its reason and attempts, and retrying one puts it back in the outbox, after which a drain delivers it.
- Ran the server locally with the publisher throwing for one topic and checked that `last_error` was filled in.
- Existing tests unchanged and passing; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are green.

## Open questions

- Should dead letters ever be purged? Right now they stay forever. I'm inclined to add a nightly job that deletes ones older than 30 days, but that's probably a separate PR.
